title: Incremental HRR vector computation via per-file content hash
description:
compute_hrr_vectors (src/similarity/mod.rs:17) re-reads every file from disk, re-parses with tree-sitter, and re-encodes ALL function/method symbols (two FFT-heavy 1024-dim encodings each, measured ~8ms/symbol) then DELETE FROM hrr_vectors + full reinsert — on every parse, regardless of what changed. Measured: 7.0s on swe_dashboard (811 fn symbols), 13.6s on sutra (1,663). This is the dominant cost of every changed-file parse (editing 2 files in sutra = 25.8s total, 14.2s of it HRR).

Fix: store the source file's content_hash alongside its vectors (per-file, atomically with the vector rows); on parse, recompute only files whose current hash differs, delete vectors only for changed/deleted files. Gate compute_pattern_families (6.2s on sutra) on "any vector changed" since its input is the vector set. Crash-safety note: hash and vectors must commit in the same transaction so an interrupted run can't record a hash for vectors it didn't write (see sutra/140 for the general completion-tracking mechanism).

Expected: changed-file parse post-parse cost drops from 8-26s to sub-second + (changed files × ~8ms/symbol).

acceptance_criteria.text: No-change parse recomputes zero HRR vectors
1-file change recomputes only that file's vectors
pattern families skipped when vector set unchanged

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review — verdict: **needs-attention** (3 high findings, all addressed in 3e847a6)

**Finding 1 [high]: Pattern families gate misses same-count edits** (src/pipeline.rs)
Count comparison fails when a file is edited but keeps the same number of functions — CASCADE removes old vectors before the count snapshot, compute_hrr_vectors inserts new ones, counts match, families skipped despite changed vector contents.
Fix: gate on `changed` flag from compute_hrr_vectors instead of count comparison.

**Finding 2 [high]: Codebook entries persist in separate transaction** (src/similarity/mod.rs)
Vectors+hashes committed before codebook entries. Crash between commits leaves vectors encoded against missing codebook entries. The codebook RNG seed depends on entry count, so lost entries change future random vectors.
Fix: include codebook entries in the same atomic transaction as vectors and file hashes.

**Finding 3 [high]: Hash written for files that failed vector generation** (src/similarity/mod.rs)
Files that fail read/adapter/parse get `continue` but their hashes still commit, permanently marking them current. Next parse skips them, leaving missing HRR vectors.
Fix: only write hash for files that successfully produced vectors (track completed_file_ids set).
